# `sngl tool cgogen` wraps a package of the program's own as it does a
# library package: it writes the Go package wrapping the package's C
# declarations into cgo/ beside it, in the program's Go module, and marks each
# declaration with its wrapper, which a //go:generate line keeps in step. A
# function taking a ref is wrapped copy-in, copy-out, a C struct with fields
# among what it fills too; the struct is a Go type of the wrapper package's,
# named so from its first generation, before a mark names it. Each handle the
# package declares is a type of the wrapper package's too, crossing a wrapped
# function or not, so a program holding one names no cgo type of its own. Two
# declarations of one C function keeping a static callback are two wrappers,
# each keeping its own function, which C calls after both were kept. The Go program calls the wrapper, reaching the program's module through its
# own, which replaces the host module with its root (codegen.WriteGoMod), and
# compiles none of the package's C, which the wrapper package does. A string
# C hands over (#[c.frees]) is freed in the wrapper, through the function its
# preamble defines, as a member of a C struct is read and called (`field`).
# A ref to an option of a pointer handle, GLib's GError **, is handed C as a
# pointer to NULL and read back null or the handle. A static callback C
# calls with a convention of its own is the static C function of that
# convention the wrapper package's callbacks define, calling the export.
# A pointer C takes as an integer typedef (#[c.type]) is cast in C, by a
# function of the preamble's the wrapper calls, as a number made a pointer
# by a cast is. A struct holding a string hands C a copy pinned for the
# call, which is not read back, and a handle read back.

# The program's module, which requires sngl from this checkout.
exec sh -c 'root="${SNGL_HOST_GO_MOD%/go.mod}"; sed "s|^module .*|module example.com/app|" "$root/go.mod" > go.mod; printf "\nreplace duckfam.us/sngl => %s\n" "$root" >> go.mod; cp "$root/go.sum" go.sum'
env SNGL_HOST_GO_MOD=$WORK/go.mod

sngl tool cgogen mathx
exists mathx/cgo/wrappers.go
exists mathx/cgo/split.c
grep '#\[go.native\("example.com/app/mathx/cgo", "cgo.SplitAdd"\)\]' mathx/mathx.sngl
grep 'func SplitAdd\(a int, b int, carry int\) SplitAddResult' mathx/cgo/wrappers.go
grep 'func SplitSwap\(p Pair\) Pair' mathx/cgo/wrappers.go
grep 'snglFree_split_free' mathx/cgo/wrappers.go
grep 'func SplitThingTwice\(t Thing, n int\) int' mathx/cgo/wrappers.go
grep 'func SplitTry\(n int, err \*Thing\) SplitTryResult' mathx/cgo/wrappers.go
grep '#\[go.native\("example.com/app/mathx/cgo", "cgo.State"\)\]' mathx/mathx.sngl
grep 'static split_wide SPLIT_CC snglStatic__widen_f_SPLIT_CC\(split_wide a0\)' mathx/cgo/callbacks.go
grep 'return split_send\(a0, \(split_param\)a1\);' mathx/cgo/wrappers.go

# A second run, reading the marks the first wrote, changes nothing.
cp mathx/mathx.sngl marked.sngl
cp mathx/cgo/wrappers.go wrappers.first
sngl tool cgogen mathx
cmp mathx/mathx.sngl marked.sngl
cmp mathx/cgo/wrappers.go wrappers.first

sngl generate --lang go --platform bubbletea -o out app.sngl
grep 'SplitAdd__result\(cgo\.SplitAdd\(7, 8, carry\)\)' out/model.go
! grep 'import "C"' out/model.go
! grep 'C\.split_state' out/model.go

sngl test --platform=bubbletea --language=go app.sngl
stdout 'ok +10 tests, 0 failures'

-- mathx/split.h --
int split_add(int a, int b, int *carry);

typedef struct {
	int lo, hi;
} split_pair;

void split_swap(split_pair *p);

typedef struct split_state split_state;

typedef int (*split_fn)(int);

// Keeps f, answering where; split_call calls what is kept there.
int split_keep(split_fn f);
int split_call(int at, int x);

// A name for n, which split_free frees; split_fill stores one in *out.
char *split_name(int n);
void split_fill(int n, char **out);
void split_free(void *p);

// What split_free freed, counted.
int split_freed(void);

// A struct a program reads the members of, and calls one of.
typedef struct split_thing {
	int code;
	int (*twice)(int n);
} split_thing;

split_thing *split_thing_new(int code);

// Answers 1 for an even n, and for an odd one stores a thing of code n in
// *err and answers 0; -1 where *err was not NULL on entry.
int split_try(int n, split_thing **err);

// x86-64's Microsoft convention, which a Linux compiler calls with only
// where it is written, and what f of it answers for 5000000000.
#define SPLIT_CC __attribute__((ms_abi))
typedef long long split_wide;
typedef split_wide (SPLIT_CC *split_wide_fn)(split_wide);
split_wide split_widen(split_wide_fn f);

// As Win32's SendMessageW: what l points to is what msg says. split_noted
// answers a thing of code 11 as such an integer.
#include <stdint.h>
typedef intptr_t split_param;
split_param split_send(int msg, split_param l);
split_param split_noted(void);

// A struct holding a string and a handle: its name's length times ten
// plus its thing's code; and, renamed, its n set to that length, its
// thing one of code n, and its name another, which the program does not
// read back.
typedef struct split_named {
	const char *name;
	split_thing *thing;
	int n;
} split_named;
int split_named_len(split_named nm);
void split_rename(split_named *nm);
-- mathx/split.c --
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>

#include "split.h"

int split_add(int a, int b, int *carry) {
	int s = a + b;
	*carry = s / 10;
	return s % 10;
}

static split_fn kept[2];
static int nkept;

int split_keep(split_fn f) {
	kept[nkept] = f;
	return nkept++;
}

int split_call(int at, int x) {
	return kept[at](x);
}

static int freed;

char *split_name(int n) {
	char *s = malloc(8);
	snprintf(s, 8, "n%d", n);
	return s;
}

void split_fill(int n, char **out) {
	*out = split_name(n);
}

void split_free(void *p) {
	freed++;
	free(p);
}

int split_freed(void) {
	return freed;
}

static int split_twice(int n) {
	return n * 2;
}

split_thing *split_thing_new(int code) {
	static split_thing t;
	t = (split_thing){code, split_twice};
	return &t;
}

int split_try(int n, split_thing **err) {
	if (*err != NULL) {
		return -1;
	}
	if (n % 2 == 0) {
		return 1;
	}
	*err = split_thing_new(n);
	return 0;
}

split_param split_send(int msg, split_param l) {
	switch (msg) {
	case 1:
		return (split_param)strlen((const char *)l);
	case 2:
		split_swap((split_pair *)l);
		return 1;
	case 3:
		return ((split_thing *)l)->code;
	}
	return 0;
}

int split_named_len(split_named nm) {
	return (int)strlen(nm.name) * 10 + nm.thing->code;
}

void split_rename(split_named *nm) {
	nm->n = (int)strlen(nm->name);
	nm->name = "zz";
	nm->thing = split_thing_new(nm->n);
}

split_param split_noted(void) {
	return (split_param)split_thing_new(11);
}

split_wide split_widen(split_wide_fn f) {
	return f(5000000000LL);
}

void split_swap(split_pair *p) {
	int lo = p->lo;
	p->lo = p->hi;
	p->hi = lo;
}
-- mathx/mathx.sngl --
import c "sngl:x/c"

c.link(include="split.h", sources=["split.c", "split.h"])

#[c.native("split_add")]
func splitAdd(a int, b int, carry ref[int]) int

#[c.native("split_pair")]
struct _Pair {
    lo int
    hi int
}

#[c.native("split_swap")]
func _swap(p ref[_Pair])

func swapped(lo int, hi int) int {
    var p = _Pair{lo=lo, hi=hi}
    _swap(&p)
    return p.lo * 10 + p.hi
}

#[c.native("split_keep")]
func _keepDoubled(#[c.type("split_fn")] #[c.static] f func(x int) int) int

#[c.native("split_keep")]
func _keepTripled(#[c.type("split_fn")] #[c.static] f func(x int) int) int

#[c.native("split_call")]
func _call(at int, x int) int

func _doubled(x int) => x * 2

func _tripled(x int) => x * 3

func applied() string {
    var d = _keepDoubled(_doubled)
    var t = _keepTripled(_tripled)
    return "{_call(d, 3)} {_call(t, 3)}"
}

// A handle no wrapped function crosses.
#[c.native("split_state *")]
struct _State {}

func stateless() bool {
    var s option[_State] = null
    return s == null
}
#[c.native("split_name")]
#[c.frees("split_free")]
func _name(n int) string

#[c.native("split_fill")]
func _fill(n int, #[c.frees("split_free")] out ref[string])

#[c.native("split_freed")]
func _freed() int

func names() string {
    var s = ""
    _fill(4, &s)
    return "{_name(3)} {s}"
}

func freed() => _freed()

#[c.native("split_thing *")]
struct _Thing {}

#[c.native("split_thing_new")]
func _thingNew(code int) _Thing

#[c.native("split_thing.code", field)]
func _code(t _Thing) int

#[c.native("split_thing.twice", field)]
func _twice(t _Thing, n int) int

func members() int {
    var t = _thingNew(7)
    return _code(t) * 100 + _twice(t, 21)
}

#[c.native("split_try")]
func _try(n int, err ref[option[_Thing]]) int

func tried() string {
    var err option[_Thing] = null
    var even = _try(2, &err)
    var none = err == null
    var odd = _try(3, &err)
    var code = 0
    if err != null {
        code = _code(err)
    }
    var again = _try(4, &err)
    return "{even} {none} {odd} {code} {again} {err == null}"
}

#[c.native("split_wide")]
struct _Wide = int

#[c.native("split_widen")]
func _widen(#[c.type("split_wide_fn")] #[c.static(convention="SPLIT_CC")] f func(n _Wide) _Wide) _Wide

func _plusOne(n int) => n + 1

func widened() => _widen(_plusOne)

#[c.native("split_param")]
struct _Param = int

#[c.native("split_send")]
func _sendText(msg int, #[c.type("split_param")] text string) _Param

#[c.native("split_send")]
func _sendPair(msg int, #[c.type("split_param")] p ref[_Pair]) _Param

#[c.native("split_send")]
func _sendThing(msg int, #[c.type("split_param")] t _Thing) _Param

#[c.native("split_noted")]
func _noted() _Param

#[c.native("split_thing *", cast)]
func _asThing(p _Param) _Thing

#[c.native("split_named")]
struct _Named {
    name  string
    thing _Thing
    n     int
}

#[c.native("split_named_len")]
func _namedLen(nm _Named) int

#[c.native("split_rename")]
func _rename(nm ref[_Named])

func named() string {
    var nm = _Named{name="abcd", thing=_thingNew(3), n=0}
    var l = _namedLen(nm)
    _rename(&nm)
    return "{l} {nm.name} {nm.n} {_code(nm.thing)}"
}

func sent() string {
    var p = _Pair{lo=3, hi=4}
    var r = _sendPair(2, &p)
    return "{_sendText(1, "abc")} {r} {p.lo}{p.hi} {_sendThing(3, _thingNew(9))} {_code(_asThing(_noted()))}"
}
-- mathx/gen.go --
package mathx

//go:generate sngl tool cgogen .
-- app.sngl --
import ui "sngl:ui"
import test "sngl:test"
import m "./mathx"

func digits() string {
    var carry = 0
    var d = m.splitAdd(7, 8, &carry)
    return "{carry}{d}"
}

ui.window(title="t") {
    ui.text("{digits()}")
}

func testItSplits(t test.Test) {
    t.assert(digits() == "15")
}

func testItSwaps(t test.Test) {
    t.assert(m.swapped(1, 2) == 21)
}

func testItAppliesEach(t test.Test) {
    t.assert(m.applied() == "6 9")
}

func testItHoldsNoState(t test.Test) {
    t.assert(m.stateless())
}

func testItReadsAndCallsMembers(t test.Test) {
    t.assert(m.members() == 742)
}

func testItFillsAnOptionOfAHandle(t test.Test) {
    t.assert(m.tried() == "1 true 0 3 1 true")
}

func testItCallsWithAConvention(t test.Test) {
    t.assert(m.widened() == 5000000001)
}

func testItSendsPointersAsIntegers(t test.Test) {
    t.assert(m.sent() == "3 1 43 9 11")
}

func testItHandsAStructHoldingAString(t test.Test) {
    t.assert(m.named() == "43 abcd 4 4")
}

func testItFreesWhatCHandsOver(t test.Test) {
    t.assert(m.names() == "n3 n4")
    t.assert(m.freed() == 2)
}
